summary.headline: Vedant Fashions Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.7% to ~INR 399 crore with 65% gross margin, while retail sales grew 7.8% to INR 561 crore and SSG was 4.6%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 retail sales (customer sales) reached about INR 561 crore, up 7.8% YoY, with SSG of about 4.6%, and management said most of the quarter's growth came in March. Reported revenue from operations was about INR 399 crore (+8.7%) and PAT about INR 114 crore (+13%). For FY26, retail sales crossed INR 2,000 crore at INR 2,008 crore (+6.1%), but revenue from operations grew only about 3.5% to INR 1,436 crore and PAT was about INR 376 crore. Management guided to mostly SSG-led growth in FY27, with gross openings stable but net store additions still positive, and said the retail-to-net-sales gap is mainly a GST effect that should normalise from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: contraction of ~150 bps per analyst question, not disputed

financial_highlights.metric: Cash conversion FY26 (operating cash flow to PAT, excl. finance income)

segments.name: Manyavar / Mohey / Twamev / Mebaz / Diwas (portfolio)
segments.commentary: Retail network of about 669 EBO stores across 252 cities and towns, totalling about 1.79 million sq ft as of March 2026. FY26 net area addition was about 4,200 sq ft after closures; gross addition was about 1 lakh sq ft. Twamev has about 8 EBOs and Mohey a similar number; Diwas has no physical stores yet.

guidance_outlook: No specific SSG guidance for FY27; management said it is targeting better SSG via footfalls, conversion, ASP and basket size.
Gross store openings to stay stable in FY27 with some consolidation; management expects net additions in FY27, with openings normalising by next financial year.
Closures could be 5-6% of retail area in FY26, versus a normal 2-3% (3-4% per another comment); management still aims for net positive sq ft growth.

Retail-to-net-sales gap (~29% for FY26, primary 71% vs secondary 73% cited) is mainly GST-driven and expected to normalise from FY27, though management said the gap is 'here to stay' at a decent level while growth rates will track.

Input cost: fabric is INR 8-10 of a INR 100 MRP product; expected 50-150 bps increase in total cost, i.e. INR 1-1.5 per INR 100 product. Management said most current SKU orders are placed at existing prices, so gross margin impact should be limited (10-15 bps at most).
Capital allocation: historically ~50% of profit paid as dividend post-IPO; a concrete policy on cash deployment is expected by the next earnings call.
Inorganic: cash is available for acquisitions, but no pipeline; management said the sector's players are too small.
capex_capacity: Gross retail area addition FY26 about 1 lakh sq ft; net addition about 4,200 sq ft after rationalising underperforming stores.
Revenue per sq ft of new stores opened vs stores closed is about 85% higher (management's average comparison for FY26).
About 5-5.5% of retail area is in underperforming stores management wants to exit.
Twamev: sites are mostly build-to-suit with 18-20 month lead time; 5-6 further stores being signed; openings staggered, with some possibly in H1 FY28 or FY29.
Manyavar kurta-only 1,000 sq ft format being piloted in high-throughput Bangalore neighbourhoods; no physical Diwas stores planned in FY27 beyond a possible pilot.
Rentals in new markets (e.g., Bhopal) are 1.3-1.4x management's target levels, which is slowing new openings.
demand_pricing: Footfall improved by low single digits in Q4 and conversion stayed stable at high levels; average basket size rose about 1.5%.
ASP growth lagged over the past 2-3 years; management plans to lift ASP by about 3-3.5% per category through merchandise upgrades, not price hikes.
Management said March was the strongest month and April has been decent; May is affected by Adhik Maas, with July wedding dates expected to help versus FY26.
Consumer sentiment turned neutral after the war began around late Feb/early March 2026.
Competitive intensity: 2022 entrants are closing, while players that entered in the last 1-2 years are still adding stores; net industry store additions are described as nil.
Gross margin contraction for FY26 attributed by management mainly to GST rate changes from September 2025 (blended GST around 10% pre-change, now slightly higher).

qa_highlights.question: How will SSG and new store openings look in FY27, and how will input inflation affect gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No SSG guidance; focus on footfall, conversion, ASP and training. Fabric is about INR 8-10 of a INR 100 product, implying 50-150 bps cost pressure, largely offset by existing orders placed at old prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the retail-to-net sales gap widened to ~29% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly GST after the September 2025 rate revision, which management expects to normalise from FY27. The growth gap between primary and secondary sales was 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: What share of stores and area is weak, and how much better are new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5-5.5% of retail area is in weak stores versus a normal closure rate of 2-3%. New stores' revenue per sq ft is about 85% higher than closed stores (FY26 averages).

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a capital return or inorganic move?
qa_highlights.answer: Historically about 50% of profit paid as dividend; a concrete policy is expected by the next call. No acquisition pipeline, though cash is available.

qa_highlights.question: Is Twamev going to scale from 8 stores to 30 in the coming year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Build-to-suit leases mean an 18-20 month lag; openings are staggered and some may come in H1 FY28 or FY29. Management declined to commit to 30 stores.

risks_watch: Revenue growth (+3.5%) lagged retail sales growth (+6.1%) in FY26, and the GST-driven gap needs to close in FY27 as management indicated.
SSG is only ~2.7% for FY26 and no FY27 target was given; watch whether footfall and ASP gains hold.
Store closures of 5-6% of retail area in FY26 and high rentals constrain net expansion.
Input cost inflation from the war (fabric and other inputs) could pressure gross margin, though management says the impact is limited.
Consumer sentiment reported as neutral since the war began; May 2026 is affected by Adhik Maas.
Capital allocation policy on the cash balance is due by the next earnings call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term positioning and AI/retention projects, but cautious on near-term demand, citing the war, neutral sentiment and Adhik Maas. Management avoided quantitative guidance on SSG, store openings and Twamev scale-up.
key_quotes: So while I can't give you a particular guidance on what SSG do we aim to achieve for the next financial year, what I can tell you is that anything and everything which we should be doing as a company to achieve better SSG numbers is something which we are targeting.
So this is one thing which we will be changing as we move ahead and focusing on improving our ASPs that would also help us improve SSGs.
So broadly, my understanding is that it should not affect our gross margins much.
Unfortunately, Rishi, the problem with Twamev EBOs is that majority of the properties we are signing are build-to-suit.

Manyavar kurta-only 1,000 sq ft format pilot in Bangalore neighbourhoods

growth.why: Management gave no numeric SSG or revenue guidance for FY27, only that growth should be mostly SSG-led with stable gross openings and positive net store additions; backing is partial (5-6 Twamev stores being signed, a kurta-only pilot, ASP plans of 3-3.5%), and FY26 revenue grew only ~3.5% against retail sales of +6.1%.
